title: Medical AI & Imaging
tagline: Work with medical images and clinical data: DICOM, segmentation with U-Net, MONAI, and nnU-Net, pathology, foundation models, bias, and regulation.
prereqs: Deep Learning. Computer Vision helps for the segmentation steps. No medical background needed.

steps.title: What makes healthcare data different
steps.why: MIT lecture on clinical data, its messiness, and its stakes.

steps.title: How ML reads medical images
steps.why: JAMA explainer on training image models against expert labels.

steps.title: Read DICOM files in Python
steps.why: Load scans and their metadata with pydicom.

steps.title: Sensitivity and specificity
steps.why: The two error rates clinicians ask about first.

steps.title: U-Net for segmentation
steps.why: The encoder-decoder with skip connections behind most medical segmentation.

steps.title: Segment organs in 3D CT
steps.why: Train a 3D segmentation model on CT scans in Python.

steps.title: nnU-Net
steps.why: A U-Net that configures its own preprocessing and training per dataset.

steps.title: Segment anything in medical images
steps.why: MedSAM adapts Segment Anything to prompt-based medical segmentation.

steps.title: Machine learning for pathology
steps.why: MIT lecture on learning from huge whole-slide tissue images.

steps.title: Foundation models in radiology
steps.why: Stanford researchers on large pretrained models for medical images and reports.

steps.title: Bias in health AI
steps.why: Where bias enters clinical models, from labels and proxies to deployment.

steps.title: How AI medical devices get cleared
steps.why: How the FDA regulates diagnostic imaging AI software in the US.

projects: Load a public CT series with pydicom, window it, and save an axial, coronal, and sagittal view.
Train a 2D U-Net on a public segmentation dataset and report Dice score per case.
Train a chest X-ray classifier and report sensitivity, specificity, and AUC on a held-out hospital split if available.
